why: A primitive-or-record union against a literal: === is true only on the literal's primitive arm holding its value, never through the coercion table. true against "true" and 1 against "1" differ (== would coerce the second pair to equal), unproved and witnessed. The literal on either side, a !== branch inverted, a typeof guard around the comparison, an explicit undefined test on an optional value and a negated number literal agree, proved; a string-or-array union is a sum compared exactly on its string arm.
